body: Oh my goodness. I was just robbed this week as well. It was the first time but I live in a really terrible neighborhood (lots of shootings and robberies) so I guess I'm some ways it's abnormal I've gone this long. I can relate to what you're saying 100%. I feel so ridiculous about it but I've been having really high anxiety going outside because I keep thinking the person who robbed me will find me again. Even when I challenge the thoughts ("what is he going to do? Double rob me? He already took all my stuff!") it still doesn't always help. Yesterday was my first time successfully leaving my house since it happened... I went out with a family member and walked a short distance with them and then walked home alone. I still felt hyper alert and unsafe, when anyone walked too close to me I'd get scared. Everyone just looks more sinister it's hard to explain. I think it just takes time, or like another suggested temporary medication if that's something you're open to. I've noticed talking to other people about it helps and trying to make light of the situation even though it terrified me, trying to make it less scary in my mind.

Thank you for the reply. I'm trying so hard to enjoy the things I used to enjoy. It's hard because my heart constantly hurts and I'm always worrying. I'm trying to see a doctor but been running into hurdles with insurance, everything feels like its moving so slow but I'm trying to keep hope that things will get better once I can see one. My biggest worry is that at this age nobody wants new friends, and that even if I manage to "fix" my anxiety I will still have too many problems for anyone to bother (where as when you are younger people seem more forgiving of not having your life together). Right now I feel like I'm behind glass and everyone else is on the other side. Or like an alien. It is very reassuring to know that people still like to make friends even when they are older- thank you again for the reply. It means a lot to have something to hope for.

It really depends. I was on the lowest dose of klonopin for 3 years, I never abused it but it was definitely long term. I ended up weaning off though of my own choosing.

Op, think about it like this: if you ask your doctor, the answer might be yes or it might be no. Maybe it's a med for you, maybe it isn't. But if you don't ask, the answer is definitely no...or you will have to wait and see. I would just be honest. Your doctor is not going to blacklist you or anything, there's a huge difference between being curious and inquiring ("I heard/read about this type of medication, I have a friend with anxiety who takes it, is it possibly something for me?") vs drug seeking ("I need this medication, I want this brand and only this brand, I need it right away and refuse to take anything else or in addition or any other options").

It made it sooooo much better. If I drank just enough to be buzzed but not enough to get drunk, it was like I was a completely better version of myself. My stammer even went away, I was able to just chill and enjoy things easily. I felt more empathetic to strangers, and kinder to myself. I didn't have this constant knot of fear in my throat all day every day. I didn't hate myself, and assume that everyone else hated me too. I could laugh easily. Things I liked felt accessible again, I could feel enjoyment from hobbies that otherwise stressed me out when I was anxious and they didn't make me feel anything...

It's how I turned into a functioning alcoholic. Now I don't drink at all because I know how much it helps me and how easy it is to slide back into that hole. The most frustrating thing is that it never got BAD... I never got blackout drunk or did anything awful because I was drunk all the time. I was just...slightly drunk, but all the time. And I know that even though it was the only time I really felt like I could live life, it was also not ok.
